author: A3 HBM group A (Claude)

ot_hbm_accel_smh_pt_w.face_pins: W/E 3,705 M4 each (10.4/um over 355 um), N/S 2,902 M5
ot_hbm_accel_smh_pt_w.note: pass-through band: height set by the 3,705-bit E-W bus on ONE horizontal pin layer (M4); std 5,407 um2

ot_hbm_accel_smh_pt_e.note: pass-through band, same 3,673-bit E-W bus; std 2,489 um2

ot_hbm_accel_smh_xs.note: x store (SRAM macros); SMMV redesign keeps it UNCHANGED (XD 128)

what_the_smmv_redesign_gives.why: SM.MATVEC redesign (el1013-hbm-redesign-smmv STEP 2) adds the x plane (XP masters + SMMV engine per cluster) OUTSIDE the SM and keeps the kernel ot_hbm_accel_smh and its x store UNCHANGED (XD 128; XD 256 would cost +13.1 mm2/die and re-harden every closed smh tile). Its cost sits outside the SM: +12,288 flops / ~+0.19 mm2 per die for landing credits and a ~66-stage relay spine per quadrant (~154k flops, ~0.45 mm2) at the r25gq v11 slice distance.

levers.lever: pass-through band on two horizontal pin layers (M4 + M6 PORT-only grant on W/E)
levers.cost: re-harden pt_w/pt_e (closed views stand until a die window names them); M6 grant from the die lead; pin assignment from the die tools

levers.lever: remove pass-through leaves entirely (buses as die/parent channel wires with relay tiles)
levers.cost: the 3,705-bit E-W bus still needs ~355 um of M4 face or channel tracks per tile column: area moves to channels, it does not vanish

verdict: NO compaction of the closed leaves reaches the 3.638 mm2 slot: even with the pass-through band deleted the remaining leaves are 4.28 mm2 (1.18x) before channels, relays, clock and PG. 16 tile clusters per SM do not fit hfd_sm; a fit needs fewer tile clusters per SM (8 -> ~3.45 mm2 of leaves with the M6 band lever) or a slot change (die / owner decision, not taken here). Even 8 tile clusters (halves SM compute: a perf/price decision) leave ~3.45 mm2 of leaves = 0.95 of the slot with no room for channels (the placed native frame is 2.2x its leaves). Realistic options: hfd_sm slot >= ~2x (32 x ~7.3 mm2 = ~233 mm2 of leaves alone on an 857 mm2 die) or fewer SMs per die.
